extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in postwar international and domestic policy
extracted.subtask_description: News dispatches about post‑World War II diplomatic, economic and domestic-administration developments (loan negotiations with the Soviet Union, UNRRA/Combined Food Board allocations, OPA price rules, departmental reorganizations). Written as Associated Press news items for a general readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. loan preconditions for Russia
rubrics_metrics.description: Russia will be asked to make major revisions in her secret economic agreements with eastern European nations if she is to get a requested $1,000,000,000 loan from the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: American officials preparing for Soviet financial mission will confront Russians with requests to: 1) revamp the five-year, exclusive 'treaties of economic collaboration' concluded with Rumania and Hungary; and 2) review short-term barter agreements signed with Poland, Yugoslavia, Czechoslovakia, Hungary. Also, U.S. notice to Moscow: general economic conditions in eastern Europe should be included in the loan talks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for U.S. protest of exclusive Soviet‑Eastern Europe treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States has protested to Moscow about these treaties on the grounds they are 'premature' because no peace treaties have been concluded and they are not in keeping with the Yalta agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials argue the pacts tend to set up a monopolistic Russian trade bloc in eastern Europe and exclude participation by other countries. Examples cited: joint banks and companies in Romania and Hungary with Russian general managers and national chairmen; contributions of seized German assets and personnel to such enterprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concerns regarding Soviet land‑use demands in Austria
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. diplomatic officials reported Russia trimmed land-use demands upon Austria from 150,000 acres to a much smaller fraction, but original demand raised grave concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for concern: 1) It would cut deeply into Austria's agricultural production potential; 2) It would indicate Soviet intent to maintain a large force there for months. U.S. has advocated a 'living off the land' restriction through UNRRA; Soviets objected and refused to vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions attached to U.S. assistance to Poland
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States moved to provide Poland a loan and surplus-purchase arrangements conditioned on Poland's pledges regarding elections and trade practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announced measures: a $40,000,000 loan for purchase of locomotives and railroad coal cars in the U.S.; arrangement to purchase up to $50,000,000 of U.S. Army surplus property in Europe. State Department emphasized Poland must fulfill commitments to hold free elections and follow nondiscriminatory trade practices (as stipulated in Yalta and Potsdam), and assured U.S. firms may operate on equal terms. Loan terms: interest at 3% annual, payments beginning 1951, semiannual installments over 20 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined Food Board / UNRRA allocation and review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Combined Food Board administers a grain pool and makes allocations for UNRRA and other needs; allocations are subject to review with significant changes in supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board increased UNRRA allocations (e.g., added supplies for famine-threatened countries). The statement notes allocations 'are subject to review with any significant changes in supplies during the year.' The board administers a pool composed largely of supplies from the U.S., Great Britain and Canada together with Argentina and Australia and may delay specific announcements pending review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific food and sugar rationing / allocation levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The Combined Food Board / UNRRA set specific per-person ration and country wheat/cereal allocations for 1946 and indicated distribution shares by country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: sugar 'five pounds per person for four months and five pounds per person for home canning in 1946.' Total world allocable supply and country allocations listed (United States 5,711,000 short tons; Canada 465,000; Great Britain 1,825,000; France 1,068,000; etc.). Allocations include exportable supply contributions from Cuba, Puerto Rico, Hawaii, Dominican Republic, British West Indies, French colonies, and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPA cigarette price adjustment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of Price Administration allowed limited increases on multi-pack and vending-machine cigarette sales but no increase for single packs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency said there will be no increase for single packs. Multiple-sales adjustments mentioned include fractional-cent increases per pack for vending and machine sales and a five-cent increase on a carton of 10 packs; exact fractional increases referenced (half cent/one cent per pack in various sale formats) in discussion of applying uniform ceilings (e.g., proposals to a uniform price of 13 cents a pack for all sales).

rubrics_metrics.name: OPA review of manufacturers' cost and production records
rubrics_metrics.description: OPA began examining suit manufacturers' cost and production records to determine whether price regulations would halt shipments after May 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPA received industry records, is 'skeptical' of claims that average price order would severely interfere with shipments, and said it would make any 'wanted adjustments' in the order. The agency expected to complete the survey within the next few days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Col. Alfred McCormack's objections to State Department reorganization
rubrics_metrics.description: In his resignation letter McCormack listed three specific reasons opposing departmental orders that dismembered the Office of Research and Intelligence and transferred its functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated reasons: 1) It will make impossible the establishment of a real intelligence unit; 2) It will weaken the department compared to military components of national intelligence authority; 3) It will prevent carrying out long-range plans for postwar intelligence. The reorganization transfers intelligence functions to separate research divisions under political offices.
